title: Constraint-solver kernel autotuner with token-phase prefill/decode switching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We observe variable latency and cost regressions across mixed conversational loads. Single-rule kernel pickers (latency-first or cost-first) fail when token-phase (prefill vs decode) and sequence-length distribution shift rapidly. This ticket implements a constraint-solver based autotuner that picks kernel variants per-request using a short horizon token-phase model and hardware-aware constraints. The solver balances multiple objectives (latency tail, median cost, memory headroom) and enforces safety constraints during prefills and decode bursts.
background_and_motivation: Existing heuristics pick kernels based on offline benchmarks and static seqlen buckets. Problems: (1) Prefill ops favor high-throughput kernels; decode favors low-latency kernels. Mixed calls (long prefill + short decode) need hybrid choices and sometimes staged switching. (2) Heterogeneous fleets with mixture of A100 and 4090-like GPUs have different occupancy sweet spots. (3) Sudden seqlen drift causes expensive kernel handoffs during live traffic. The constraint-solver approach encodes SLOs, memory safety, and switching cost, then computes a per-request plan (pick or staged-swap) constrained to quick decision budgets.
proposal_summary: Build a lightweight constraint-solver module in the runtime that: (a) consumes per-request features (arch fingerprint, input_length, prefix_length, requested_max_tokens, cold/warm KV cache flag), (b) consults an online cost surface cache (microbenchmarks + telemetry extrapolations), (c) solves a small MILP-ish problem with time budget (<=500us) to select either a single kernel or a 2-stage kernel plan (prefill kernel K1, switch-to kernel K2 at decode start). Fallback to default heuristic if solver times out. Integrate telemetry to record solver choices and outcome for continual retraining of the cost surface.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime can make kernel selection decisions for 99% of requests within 500us on CPU worker. 2) End-to-end median latency improves or cost reduces by >=5% on mixed conversational benchmark compared to baseline heuristic. 3) No increase in OOM incidents in staged switching experiments. 4) Telemetry schema emitted and dashboards created: solver_choice, solver_latency_us, predicted_cost, observed_cost, switch_occurrence.
tasks: Design constraint model and decision variables (prefill-only, decode-only, staged-switch).
Implement solver service library (C++ runtime module + thin gRPC/IPC API).
Add microbenchmark harness for candidate kernels with token-phase labeling.
Integrate cost-surface cache read/write with TTL and decay heuristics.
Wire telemetry events and create dashboard queries for solver performance and safety signals.
End-to-end canary in dedicated pool with A/B: solver-on vs heuristic baseline.
Document failure modes and auto-fallback rules in runtime config.
Create postmortem checklist for staged-switch regressions.
Ship runtime-1.19 feature flag guarded rollout and runtime config knobs.
tech_notes:
- Kernel variants considered: flash-attn-2-blocked, flash-attn-1-streaming, tiled-causal-small-bsz, low-memory-int8-decode.
- Cost model inputs: single-token decode latency, per-token throughput during prefill, transient memory peak, switch_overhead_ms (measured for cache transfers).
- Safety constraints: estimated_memory_peak + safety_margin <= GPU_available_memory; switch_overhead_ms < decode_latency_budget; predicted_latency_p95 <= p95_slo + slack.
- Solver strategy: greedy MILP relaxation with one-integer decision (choose staged or not) then continuous allocation; fallback to bandit heuristic if solver fails.
- Implementation language: C++ for hot path; Python/callable harness for offline tuning jobs.
- Decision cache: store mapping of (arch_fingerprint, seqlen_bucket, prefix_ratio_bucket) -> greedy choice to avoid repeated solves for heavy tails.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for solver correctness against synthetic cost surfaces.
- Microbenchmarks across supported GPUs to populate cost-surface initial table.
- Smoke tests for staged switch path including KV cache transfer and token alignment.
- Load test synthetic mixed-workload: 40% long prefill (>=1024), 60% short prefill with decode bursts to simulate chat.
- Canary rollout in dedicated pool (1% traffic) for 48h, monitor latencies, OOM, error rates.
- Run offline replay on 7 days of traffic to estimate predicted vs observed savings.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: (1) experiment mode (read-only, log decisions) for 2 days to validate predictions, (2) limited canary (5 reserved GPUs in dedicated pool) for 72h with auto-rollback on safety metric breach, (3) gradual ramp to 25% of reserved capacity, (4) full enabling subject to SLO compliance. Include kill-switch by config and fallback reward to baseline heuristic.
measurements_and_metrics: Primary: delta median latency, delta p95 latency, per-token cost delta. Safety: OOM count, switch_failure_rate, solver_timeout_rate. Operation: solver_cpu_us distribution, telemetry coverage percent. Dashboard: runtime-1.19 / kernel-autotune / solver-health.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: solver introduces added decision latency impacting tail. Mitigation: hard 500us budget and decision cache, fallback to baseline.
- Risk: staged switching causes KV inconsistencies. Mitigation: enforce atomic handoff, add tests, and initial canary limited to non-critical customers.
- Risk: inaccurate cost surface for new GPU types. Mitigation: conservative safety margins and offline profiling jobs on new archs before ramp.
